items.prose: `rets` has columns `stock`, `mkt` and `ret`. A stock with fewer than 3 days should give NaN.
items.question: Which expression returns one beta per stock?

options.text: `rets.groupby("stock").apply(lambda g: np.cov(g.mkt, g.ret)[0, 1] / g.mkt.var() if len(g) > 2 else np.nan, include_groups=False)`
`rets.groupby("stock").apply(lambda g: np.cov(g.mkt, g.ret)[0, 1] / np.var(g.mkt) if len(g) > 2 else np.nan, include_groups=False)`
options.why: You mixed divisors: `np.cov` divides by $n - 1$ and `np.var` by $n$, so every beta is off by $n/(n-1)$.

options.text: `rets.groupby("stock").apply(lambda g: np.cov(rets.mkt, rets.ret)[0, 1] / rets.mkt.var() if len(g) > 2 else np.nan, include_groups=False)`
options.why: You used `rets`, not `g`, so every stock gets the same pooled beta.

options.text: `for s, g in rets.groupby("stock"): beta = np.cov(g.mkt, g.ret)[0, 1] / g.mkt.var() if len(g) > 2 else np.nan`
options.why: You overwrite `beta` on each pass, so only the last stock's survives.

feedback.correct: Cov over var, per group, guarded.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Check which frame each expression reads and how it divides.

byKey.last: It keeps only the last result.

explain.text: The beta is $\text{cov}(m, r)/\text{var}(m)$ inside each group. Both use $n - 1$ in `np.cov` and `.var()`.
